# SOURCE: Visual Genome 1.4 object attributes (aggregated)

- Dataset: Visual Genome, Krishna et al., "Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations", IJCV 2017. Files `attributes.json.zip` (v1.2/1.4 attributes, 83 MB zipped, 463 MB unzipped, dated 2016-08-30) and `attribute_synsets.json.zip`.
- Original hosts: `https://visualgenome.org/static/data/dataset/` and `https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~ranjaykrishna/visualgenome/data/dataset/`. Both were checked on 2026-11-15. The washington.edu files return 404. The visualgenome.org domain no longer belongs to the project and now serves an unrelated gambling site.
- Fetched from: the verbatim mirror of the original zips on Hugging Face, `https://huggingface.co/datasets/jn12/VisualGenome` (files `attributes.json.zip`, `attribute_synsets.json.zip`). Its card says `license: cc-by-4.0`. The canonical HF dataset `ranjaykrishna/visual_genome` also says `license: cc-by-4.0`. Fetched 2026-11-15.
- Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ , as published by the Visual Genome project. Attribution: "Visual Genome (Krishna et al., 2017), CC BY 4.0". No NC, ND or research-only clause.
- How it was cut: the 463 MB file was aggregated in a scratch directory, and only the aggregate is committed. The input has 108,077 images and 3,802,374 objects; 1,674,166 of those objects have at least one attribute. For each object, the key is its first synset (`object_synset`, empty when none is given: 139,659 rows) and its first name (`object_name`). Names and attributes are lowercased with whitespace collapsed, and an attribute is counted once per object. Each row counts the objects carrying that attribute. `attribute_synset` comes from Visual Genome's own `attribute_synsets.json` map (empty when the map has no entry: 90,419 rows). Every pair is kept, singletons included (2,342,302 object–attribute pairs in all).
- File: `object-attributes.tsv`: 439,318 rows, 15.9 MB, sorted by count descending. Columns: object_synset, object_name, attribute, attribute_synset, count. 135,315 rows have count >= 2. The singletons are noisy crowd annotations (free text such as "made of bricks" or "far away"), so filter by count when you import. Candidate facts only; import after review.
